method: Hold topic IDs and observed source populations fixed at the version recorded with each observation. Treat joins, category splits and cross-listing as hypothetical until original video/aggregate-level records and a compatible source frame support exact classifications and non-overlapping units.

candidate_overlap_examples.original_population: Online animation fans aged 14–24, n=358, who watch animated series created for YouTube weekly or more
candidate_overlap_examples.reason: A selected online animation-fan survey is not individually classified into child-directed versus anime or all animation audience groups.

candidate_overlap_examples.original_population: Videos with both halloween and makeup in the title
candidate_overlap_examples.reason: A beauty title-keyword view sample cannot be reassigned into styling, fashion or personal lifestyle audiences without video-level inclusion records.

candidate_overlap_examples.original_population: Videos related to Minecraft; cumulative lifetime
candidate_overlap_examples.reason: All videos related to Minecraft are not the same as organized esports and cannot be allocated by sport-like competitive status.
Platform-defined news watch-time cannot be split into political reporting and commentary without validated video labels, and viewer ideology cannot be inferred.

change_categories.condition: Same definition, only presentation label changes
New buckets partition old membership in a validated underlying microdata or joint table
Source categories' identity and overlap must be measured before aggregation
Same video may belong to more than one content taxonomy
Old ID retained as historical definition and linked to a new vocabulary

change_policy: Never overwrite or delete an existing historical observation on the basis of a newly preferred label.
Keep old source scope, original title/keyword predicate and original metric definition alongside a published taxonomy version.
A topical video-views aggregate cannot turn into a count of distinctive people, active creators or a newly split category without matching underlying records.
If split labels overlap, do not sum or assign percentages unless true overlap or mutually exclusive records are measured.
An adult or child audience classification is not inferred from animation format or a channel title.
Political article labels and actual viewer political identity are different concepts; no personal partisan profiling.
No change of the existing 33 topic IDs or reassignment of existing 36 source observations is performed by this protocol.
All unmeasured recoding fractions stay null and are not represented as zeros.

post_baseline_source_observations.original_population: YouTube views of publisher-defined videos related to the South Korean original animated series Alien Stage; report is a franchise-specific selection, not all independent animation
post_baseline_source_observations.note: An additional newly sourced observation after the frozen original 36, without relabeling any baseline row or changing the original 33 topics.
